# `starhermit:draw`

Engine **1.40.0** (host API 1.40), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:draw";
```

The per-frame 2D overlay over the 3D scene (HUDs), drawn in call order and cleared as each frame begins; call it from `onUpdate` or `onRender`. Coordinates are window pixels from the top-left corner. At most 65,536 items a frame (16,384 before API\_MINOR 21's runtime), 4,096 characters a text and 65,536 characters a frame (RangeError). The runtime's own interface always draws above it. The frame's overlay draws at most 524,288 vertices (three a triangle; 262,144 before): a frame past them draws none of its overlay (the console says so once: "2D vertex budget exceeded"). An image, rectangle or line is six vertices, so the most items fit whole as images (393,216 vertices, about 12 MiB a frame sent to the GPU). `box` is the costly item: a plain box takes a few dozen vertices, a gradient a few hundred, and a repeating radial gradient a ring at each stop of each period (about 5,200 for hard rings every 10 pixels over a 120-pixel box, so about a hundred such boxes fill the budget).

Busy views (a large isometric map, thousands of units): every item is CPU work in the game's call and on the runtime's drawing thread each frame, so draw what does not change once and reuse it. Draw static layers (terrain, roads, buildings) into an OffscreenCanvas when they change and draw that canvas each frame as one item (or several tiles of at most 4,096 pixels a side); keep sprites in a few sheets and draw each with `image`'s `source` rather than a canvas or texture apiece (each image counts against `budgets().textures`, and consecutive items from one image with one blend draw as one batch); cull what is off screen before drawing it; and move a scene of many like objects to `starhermit:scene` (InstancedMesh, Sprite), which the GPU draws without an item each.

Fonts. Text in no family the game added draws with the operating system's fonts, as browsers map the generic families: `system-ui` (the default; Segoe UI on Windows, DejaVu Sans on Linux), `sans-serif` (Arial, Liberation Sans or DejaVu Sans), `serif`, `monospace`, `cursive` and `fantasy`; characters a face lacks take the next face that has them (other system families, Segoe UI Symbol on Windows), and the engine's 5 × 7 pixel font (`starhermit pixel`, printable ASCII, `· × — …` and the arrows) comes last, so a machine without system fonts still draws ASCII. On common systems that covers Latin-1, Latin Extended-A and general punctuation (`é`, `ß`, `–`, `’`); symbols such as `★` depend on the system. Besides its own emoji font (below), the runtime ships no font file and reads fonts only from the system's font directories; games name them only by the generic families (a system family's own name, such as `Arial`, is not a family here, so text cannot tell which fonts the system has). Exact metrics (widths, line heights) differ between systems, as on the web: measure text (`measureText`) rather than assume widths.

Emoji draw in colour from the engine's own emoji font, StarHermit Emoji, the same on every system and in browsers: in `text` and `measureText` here, in `starhermit:ui`, and in a canvas's `fillText` and `measureText` (`strokeText` strokes an emoji's outline in the stroke style, as browsers do). It comes after every other face, just before the pixel font, except that an emoji drawn in emoji style by default (Emoji\_Presentation, such as `😀 🔴 ⭐`) takes it over a system face's black-and-white form, as browsers prefer their emoji font. U+FE0F after a character asks for emoji style (`❤️`, where `❤` alone is text style), U+FE0E for text style; neither draws anything. Without either, an emoji that is text style by default (`❤ 🛤 ⚖`) draws with the first face that has it, as browsers do, so a system face's black-and-white form where one has it (Segoe UI Symbol on Windows has `🛤`): write U+FE0F (`🛤️`) to have the emoji font's colour form everywhere. An emoji's own colours draw whatever the text's color (its opacity still applies), except parts the font gives the text's color (as it draws text-style symbols such as `✔ ☀`, also after U+FE0F, except `⚖️ ✖️`, which have colour forms). It also has symbols that Unicode gives no emoji form (`⌖ ☆ ✓ ● ⚀`), drawn in the text's color, and like any face draws them wherever no face before it has them (loading for them as for emoji). The font is original art, under the engine's licence, and has 833 glyphs: the common single emoji, one code point each (an emoji it lacks draws with the faces before it, or as the pixel font's box), and the twelve keycaps (`0`–`9`, `#` or `*`, U+FE0F, U+20E3: `2️⃣ #️⃣`, also without the U+FE0F), each one key drawn the same everywhere. U+20E3 never draws on its own: anywhere else the character before it draws as plain text. This version draws no other emoji sequences: in a ZWJ sequence (`👩‍💻`) each emoji draws on its own and the joiner draws nothing, a skin-tone modifier is dropped (the emoji draws in its default tone), and a flag draws as its two regional indicator letters where a face has them. The font loads the first time text needs it, never before (a game without emoji never loads it): until it arrives, which takes a moment in a browser, emoji (and its symbols that no other face has) draw as nothing in the room they take once it is in (an em each), so text keeps its layout, and then they draw. Nothing waits or throws. A canvas keeps what it drew, so emoji a canvas's `fillText` drew before the font arrived stay blank there (natively too, where it reads the font from disk in a moment): a game that bakes emoji into a canvas once waits for `fonts.load(font, text)` from `starhermit:canvas` first (since engine 1.20.1), as on the web. Since API\_MINOR 37 (`EMOJI_FAMILY_MINOR`) a game can name the font as a family, `StarHermit Emoji` (any case; quoted in a canvas `font`): a canvas's `font` (`"48px 'StarHermit Emoji', sans-serif"`), `text`'s `font` here, a `starhermit:ui` text `font` and `setFont`, and a `TextLabel`'s `font`. Text in it draws every character the font has with the font's glyph (in emoji or text style as above), ahead of any system face, so symbols such as `● ▲ ■ ◆ ★ ✚ ◐ ⬡ → ✓` look the same on every system, natively and in browsers; the characters it lacks (ASCII letters and digits, spaces, most punctuation) draw with the faces after it in a canvas font list, else with `sans-serif` (for `text` and UI text, always `sans-serif`) and then the pixel font. As the first family it sets the line's metrics (ascent 1900 and descent 500 of 2048 units an em). A family the game adds under the same name is its own, as any added family is. Older minors' text naming it draws as an unknown family does (`sans-serif`; a UI `font` throws). Text in the default and generic families is unchanged at every minor: an emoji in emoji style already draws with this font on every system (the runtime loads no system colour font), while a character that is text style by default (`★ → ©`) draws with the first face that has it, as in browsers, so the system's where it has one; name the family for the same glyph everywhere.

### Clip

*interface*

```ts
export interface Clip { … }
```

- `clip?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };`

  Only the part inside this window rectangle draws.

### BlendMode

*type*

```ts
export type BlendMode = "normal" | "add" | "multiply" | "screen";
```

How an item combines with what is drawn under it (since API\_MINOR 18), as canvas composites: `normal` (`source-over`, the default), `add` (canvas `"lighter"`: colors added, for glows and additive particles; two overlapping half-bright items make a full one), `multiply` (darkens; canvas's own over the opaque frame) and `screen` (lightens). Items of different blends draw in call order, the same natively and in browsers. Another name is a TypeError.

### box

*function*

```ts
export function box(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, style: string | readonly string[] | import("starhermit:ui").Style, options?: Clip): void;
```

A box drawn as `starhermit:ui` draws a styled widget's (since API\_MINOR 12), for HUD pieces drawn by hand (a pill over the world, a gradient frame): `style` is class names registered with `ui.setStyles` (a string or an array) or a style object, of which the box properties draw (fills, border, radius, shadows, decorations, opacity, translate). The rectangle is window pixels; the style's sizes are logical, at the UI's scale, and the player's high contrast applies as to widgets. It counts as one overlay item per part it draws.

### PathOptions

*interface*

A path's look (`draw.path`). `fill`, `stroke` or both (TypeError without either); the fill is drawn first.

```ts
export interface PathOptions extends Clip, Rotation, Blend { … }
```

- `fill?: ColorLike;`
- `stroke?: ColorLike;`

- `lineWidth?: number;`

  The stroke's width in path units (1), so scaled with the path as SVG's `stroke-width` and a canvas's under `scale()`; 0 or less strokes nothing.

- `scale?: number;`

  Window pixels a path unit (1); negative mirrors, 0 draws nothing.

- `fillRule?: "nonzero" | "evenodd";`

  `"nonzero"` (default) or `"evenodd"`, as canvas's `fill(rule)`.

- `lineCap?: "butt" | "round" | "square";`

  As canvas's: `"butt"` (default), `"round"`, `"square"`.

- `lineJoin?: "miter" | "round" | "bevel";`

  As canvas's: `"miter"` (default), `"round"`, `"bevel"`.

- `miterLimit?: number;`

  As canvas's (10; one not above 0 is ignored).

### path

*function*

```ts
export function path(d: string, x: number, y: number, options: PathOptions): void;
```

SVG path data filled and stroked in the overlay (since API\_MINOR 37, `DRAW_PATH_MINOR`; undefined for games declaring an older `engine.minor`): the icons and glyphs games kept as SVG sprites, with holes, curves and arcs, as `new Path2D(d)` reads them (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A and Z, absolute and relative, implicit repetition; drawn up to the data's first error as SVG draws it). The path's point (px, py) lands at (x + px × scale, y + py × scale), then `rotation` turns it about `origin` (window pixels, default (x, y)) as the other items turn; `clip` and `blend` as theirs. The data is parsed and flattened (curves within 0.1 window pixels at the scale drawn) by canvas's code natively, and the fill (by `fillRule`) and the stroke (canvas's joins and caps) cut into triangles that do not overlap, so a translucent path blends once everywhere, crossings and overlapping subpaths included; edges are not antialiased (as `polygon`'s and `line`'s). One overlay item a call. The triangles are kept per data and scale (by powers of two, every scale's own tolerance; a curve takes at most 4,096 chords), so drawing the same path each frame parses it once; a path not kept costs fuel for its parse, flattening, stroke and sweep as they run, a refused one too. Limits: 65,536 bytes of data (RangeError), 16,384 segments and points flattened, 65,536 vertices drawn, a sweep's work (RangeErrors).

### Rotation

*interface*

Turns a text or image about `origin` (default its top-left corner, in window pixels; a circle, ellipse or arc about its center).

```ts
export interface Rotation { … }
```

- `rotation?: number;`

  Radians, clockwise on screen.

- `origin?: { x: number; y: number };`

Circles, ellipses and arcs (since API\_MINOR 18), their edges antialiased over a pixel as `roundRect`'s, the same natively and in browsers, as smooth as their size needs (no point limit). Each is one overlay item. A negative radius is a RangeError; a radius of 0 or a `lineWidth` of 0 draws nothing. Outlines are centered on the curve (as canvas strokes it; `strokeRect` draws inside), `lineWidth` default 1, an arc's ends cut square (canvas's butt caps). Angles are radians from +x, clockwise on screen (canvas's), an ellipse's parametric as canvas's `ellipse`.

### TextOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface TextOptions extends Clip, Rotation { … }
```

- `size?: number;`

  Pixels (default 16).

- `color?: ColorLike;`

- `font?: string;`

  A family added with `canvas.fonts`, a generic family (`system-ui`, the default, `sans-serif`, `serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`) or `starhermit pixel` (the pixel font, crisp at multiples of 10), or since API\_MINOR 37 `StarHermit Emoji` (the engine's emoji font first, then `sans-serif`: see "Emoji" above); any other name draws as `sans-serif`, as browsers fall back. The system's own families (Arial, DejaVu Sans) are reached only through the generic families.

- `align?: "start" | "center" | "end";`

  Where `x` is: the text's start (default), center or end.

- `weight?: FontWeight;`

  A `FontFace` weight of the family (`"bold"`, `700`, `"700"`); the nearest face added under it (or the system's bold face) is used; a family without a bold face draws a synthesized bold at 600 and more, its glyphs emboldened as Chrome emboldens them (1/24 to 1/32 em wider) on the regular's advances, so it measures as the regular does.

- `letterSpacing?: number;`

  Extra pixels between characters (within ±1,024).

- `shadow?: { color: ColorLike; x: number; y: number };`

  Drawn first under the text, offset by `x`/`y` pixels.

- `stroke?: { color: ColorLike; width?: number };`

  An outline around each glyph under the fill, as canvas's `strokeText` then `fillText` draw outlined text (since API\_MINOR 18): `width` pixels (default 1, at most 32, RangeError; 0 draws none) centered on the glyphs' edges, so half of it shows past them, with round joins; over the shadow. It bakes into an image once for each text, size and width (a changing text, a score, once a value), and the text stays one text item (play scripts match it once).

- `maxWidth?: number;`

  Wrap at this width in pixels. With `align: "center"`, since API\_MINOR 38 (`TEXT_LINE_CENTER_MINOR`) each wrapped line is centred on `x` on its own, as CSS's `text-align: center`; before it the lines start together and the block (its widest line) is centred.

- `direction?: "ltr" | "rtl";`

### text

*function*

```ts
export function text(text: string, x: number, y: number, options?: TextOptions): void;
```

`y` is the top of the first line.

### measureText

*function*

```ts
export function measureText(text: string, options?: Pick<TextOptions, "size" | "font" | "weight" | "letterSpacing" | "maxWidth" | "direction" | "stroke">): { width: number; height: number };
```

The size `text` draws at with these options: the same faces (the weight's), letter spacing, wrap width and direction, so a width measured here is the width drawn. Drawing is unscaled: this follows neither the player's interface size nor their text size. To lay out `starhermit:ui` widgets, measure with `ui.measureText`, which does. With a `stroke` (since API\_MINOR 18) both grow by its width, the outline reaching half of it past each side (the text's fill stays where it draws without one).

### ImageOptions

*interface*

`blend` since API\_MINOR 18 (an additive glow sprite: `"add"`).

```ts
export interface ImageOptions extends Clip, Rotation, Blend { … }
```

- `source?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };`

  Part of the source in its own pixels (default all of it). As canvas's `drawImage` takes it: a part reaching past the image is clipped to it and the destination shrinks with it (the image is never stretched past its edge), a negative width or height spans the other way, and a part with no area in the image draws nothing.

- `tint?: ColorLike;`

  Multiplies the image (default white).

### image

*function*

```ts
export function image(source: Texture | OffscreenCanvas | ImageBitmap, x: number, y: number, width?: number, height?: number, options?: ImageOptions): void;
```

Draws a texture, canvas (as it is now) or bitmap; the width and height default to the source's size. A canvas or bitmap takes one of the game's images (`budgets().textures`, 120 unless raised) from the first frame it is drawn; see `Budgets` for when it goes and what a full budget does.
